pattern.top_pattern: ME facility spending is being pushed by acute hospital pricing and smaller rehab growth
pattern.what_is_impacting: ME acute hospital HMO and physical rehab PPO facility spend
pattern.pattern_details: ME shows two facility cost issues with different profiles. The larger issue is an acute hospital HMO price spike on a very small base, while the smaller PPO physical rehab increase reflects both more claims and higher paid per case. The business response should separate claim-level pricing validation from broader contract and utilization action.
pattern.why_it_matters: ME facility trend can be overstated by a single high-cost acute event unless pricing is validated before broader network action.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Validate the high-cost acute hospital HMO claim at the claim-pricing level first, then review PPO physical rehab reimbursement and utilization controls as a second action.
pattern.validation_reason: The acute hospital component is a small-base unit-cost spike with no claim growth, so repricing validation is needed before treating it as a contract trend.
evidence_summary: ME facility cost pressure totaled +$643K across HMO acute hospital and PPO physical rehab.
Acute hospital HMO contributed +$485K with no claim growth, indicating pure unit cost pressure on a very small base.
PPO physical rehab added +$158K on +99 claims with about +$1.5K higher paid per case.
